science.title: A neuro-symbolic framework for cross-hospital glaucoma detection from fundus images
science.description: In 2020, an estimated 79.6 million people were affected by glaucoma, which is expected to increase to 111.8 million by 2040. Early identification is critical, but most automatic detection systems do not generalize well across hospitals and imaging devices. In this paper, we present the neuro-symbolic glaucoma detection framework (NSC), which combines an efficient network (EfficientNet-B4) using dual spatial-channel attention, a six-node anatomical graph attention network (GAT-GNN), and a differentiable symbolic constraint module that applies four clinical fuzzy logic rules involving cup-to-disc ratio (CDR), rim thinning, defects in retinal nerve fiber layer (RNFL), and vessel density. The framework is trained on 9100 fundus images drawn from a curated corpus of 12,619 images across eight datasets and eight countries. The 12,134 non-holdout images were split 75%/12.5%/12.5% into 9100 training, 1517 validation and 1517 test images; the 485-image RIM-ONE DL set was held out entirely as a never-seen cross-hospital test set. Augmentation is applied during training and does not alter the number of distinct images in any split. Among the evaluated variants the highest cross-hospital AUC is obtained by EfficientNet-B4+Symbolic (B4, 0.6997, 95% CI 0.649–0.750); the differences between B2, B3 and B4 on the cross-hospital holdout are small and not statistically significant. EfficientNet-B4+GAT-GNN (B3) is proposed as the deployment configuration on the basis of in-distribution performance and inference cost rather than cross-hospital AUC. The full NSC model achieves a test AUC of 0.946 (95% CI 0.934–0.958) and sensitivity of 0.900, while B3 achieves the highest in-distribution AUC among the evaluated variants at 0.9612 (95% CI 0.951–0.972). Ablation studies show that adding the GAT-GNN to EfficientNet-B4 improved in-distribution test AUC by 1.4 percentage points in the single-seed ablation (0.9472–0.9612) and the performance of GNN-symbolic interaction in terms of cross-hospital AUC is reduced by 8.1 points (z = − 3.08, p = 0.002). Across three independent training runs (seeds 42, 1337, and 2024), B3 achieved a mean test AUC of 0.9602 ± 0.0002, compared with 0.9492 ± 0.0015 for B2. On images excluded from training, agreement between the CDR proxy and expert-measured cup-to-disc ratio is weak and inconsistent across datasets ($$\rho = 0.549$$, $$n = 26$$ on DRISHTI-GS; $$\rho = 0.081$$, $$n = 100$$ on REFUGE2), so anatomical grounding of the CDR proxy is not established. Validation of the CDR, RNFL, rim and vessel latent representations against segmentation ground truth remains future work. To the best of the authors’ knowledge, this is the first neuro-symbolic framework for glaucoma detection from fundus images, combining differentiable fuzzy constraints with anatomical graph reasoning, evaluated in a strict cross-hospital holdout setting (Canon CR-2 to Nidek AFC-210) without using segmentation masks.

science.title: Novel application of artificial intelligence based astronomical centroiding to small particle tracking
science.description: Quantitative assessment of aerosol particle size distribution is an important variable for evaluating barrier mask efficacy and mitigating airborne pathogen transmission. However, real world aerosol imaging is compromised by optical noise, such as light scatter, background interference and variable illumination, limiting the reliability of conventional testing approaches. Herein, we propose a novel solution to this issue centred on star centroiding, an astronomy-derived approach built on two deep learning models, MobileUNet and ELUNet. These models were originally trained on noisy images to detect celestial objects, which resemble aerosol particles. The models were applied without retraining to laser-illuminated aerosol images acquired during mask efficacy experiments. These images were generated by laser illumination of aerosol produced from a 10% NaCl-in-water solution and exhaled through a medical mannequin connected to an artificial lung, with the dataset comprising both constant and plume emission conditions. Across 41 images containing 7,123 manually annotated aerosol particles, MobileUNet detected 99% (model-to-manual ratio) of all manually annotated aerosol particles and achieved 98% for precision, recall, and F1-score, whereas ELUNet detected 97% of particles with precision, recall, and F1-score of 98%, 96%, and 97%, respectively. MobileUNet additionally reduced computation time by approximately four-fold compared to ELUNet. These findings demonstrate that astronomical centroiding models can be directly translated to aerosol analysis maintaining high performance in real life uncontrolled and high-noise environments. This interdisciplinary approach provides a robust framework for aerosol quantification and objective assessment of mask efficacy, with potential applications in pandemic preparedness and airborne infection control.
